messages:
maria: Quick handoff — I'm stepping offline at ~17:50 PT. Main things to watch:
- DB migration kicked at 17:10, ETA ~18:10. Watch for 500s on /v1/embed and schema-lock warnings.
- Canary rolling 3.2.1 at 10% (latency might bump).
- Redis eviction spike earlier cleared but eviction rate ~= 0.6% (if it drifts >1% start cache-warm job).
Action items: @sam watch canary, @chen verify migration finish, @rachel merge #432 when CI green. Ping me for escalations :wave:

oncall-bot: Reminder: shift ending for maria at 18:00 PT. Primary handoff -> @sam.

sam: Acknowledged. I'll watch canary for the next 60m. If p50 > 220ms or error rate >0.5% I'll initiate staged rollback (5% -> 0% -> full). Setting a quick monitor: `monitor set canary-latency --threshold 220`

chen: Migration update: 65% complete, no table locks. Hiccup on index creation step — switching to `CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY` to avoid lock. If that fails fallback is ALTER TABLE with short maintenance window. Will report back in 15m.

rachel: PR #432 rerun CI due to flaky test. ETA ~30m. If anyone needs the new metrics before merge, use the `metrics/metrics-db` dashboard (temp link).

maria: FYI started a background cache-warm at 17:30, throttled to 2rps to avoid API rate limits. If eviction creeps up, pause it.

sam: Quick question — if latency rises slightly, are we okay doing a partial rollback to 5% instead of full rollback to reduce blast radius?

maria: Yes, prefer staged rollback plan: drop to 5% first then to 0% then rollback. Escalate if error rate > 0.8% or p50 > 300ms.

chen: Migration finished at 17:58 — no errors. Verified new schema columns present and ran basic smoke checks against embed route. Removing migration locks now.

oncall-bot: Event logged: migration-complete @1765439500

rachel: CI rerun passed, merging shortly. @maria will surface the new metric to the prod dashboard after merge?

maria: Yup, merge and promote to prod dashboard when ready.

sam: Watching dashboards now — p50 ~210ms, error ~0.3%, looks stable. Taking primary pager. Alias page -> sam.

chen: Quick troubleshooting note (leaving in thread): if you see slow queries check `SELECT pid, now() - query_start AS duration, state, query FROM pg_stat_activity WHERE state <> 'idle';` — last time we saw long idle-in-transaction.

rachel: Got it, thanks. All good from observability side. Happy handoff, have a good evening everyone :coffee:

maria: Thanks team — I'm offline. Oncall doc updated with these notes: https://redwood.internal/oncall/notes/1765439999
